title: Phantasia - Grid Crawler Feedback
author: Epyx911
selftext:
Hi All,  been working on improving workflows and art cohesion. Looking for feedback on how things are looking at this stage? 

The game is a combination of Bard's Tale/Alternate Reality the City and Grimrock but turn based like those older games and Wizardry style combat.

I have built a full game editor for it to made additional adventures and campaigns but it comes with an initial full campaign that so far clocks in at about 30 hours for a straight run and 50 for completionist run.

Workflows:

ChatGPT with [Meshy.ai](http://Meshy.ai) to create the 3d Models and then Opus 5.5 to animate (Idle/attack/miss/hit/cast animations for all monsters). 

Suno for music including the track in this video.

ChatGPT and PhotoShop for UI work...inventory is drag and drop paper doll and i always liked the Etrian menu system so styled it after that in terms of how it flows.

I have tried to go for a cohesive stylized look...and its all a WIP just looking for feedback on current state.

Let me know your thoughts on what could be improved...what you would need to see more of to judge the aesthetics etc.

Thanks in advance!

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
The UI is a bit busy, and I think there surely has to be a better way of showing front row / back row? 

The characters have that 'generic fantasy' problem. And you'll probably push back with, 'but I LIKE generic fantasy!', and sorry but that's not an excuse. There's a difference between enjoying and celebrating the tropes of D&D/Pathfinder vs just cranking out a generic-looking Orc, Dwarf and Elf from an LLM. Those portraits have no personality to them.   


Like, look at Merisiel, Valaros and Harsk. It's a human warrior, an elf rogue and a dwarf ranger, but you can immediately get a sense of who they are - or at least immediately become interested in who they are - just from looking at their images. 

  
There's a lot of this problem with the images people are generating. A character doesn't just 'look AI' because an LLM made it - it looks AI because there's nothing to the character. 'Make me an orc. And IDK, give him armor I guess? Done'. 

  
Looking on your map... it looks like there is just a LOT of territory to maze through. Is there meaningful content for the player to engage with in all of that space? Or is it going to feel empty?

A huge mistake so many developers make is thinking that they need a big world that they don't have enough content for, when in fact the far better approach is to aim for a small world that will feel alive and huge because it is sized appropriately to the content within it.

replies.author: Epyx911
replies.body:
Awesome. Love it. Thanks very much.  You are right the front row back row is very 80s Wizardry...I can probably figure out a way to actually put front ahead visually...again great food for thought...will work on this.

The portraits were from a Unity asset pack and the claim was no AI. I will try to find some that have more character...again great feedback. Thank you!

Here is a 3d model (quest giver/NPC) for the town...what are your thoughts on the end look.

Here is my master style prompt for the 3d models:

Stylized hand-painted medieval fantasy character in the style of the reference images, full body from head to toe, seen from the front, standing straight in a T-pose with the arms held straight out to the sides, hands open and empty with the fingers slightly apart, feet slightly apart and flat on the ground, neutral face with the mouth closed, looking straight ahead. One character alone, plain light grey background, soft even lighting, no shadow, no text. Clear gaps between the arms and the body and between the legs. A game character model reference

A weary working woman in her forties, a tanner's widow, thin and red-eyed, dark hair tied back under a plain black kerchief. A long faded black dress with the sleeves rolled to the elbows, a heavy leather apron stained pale with lime, worn wooden clogs
